analysis.evidence: עֶרֶב is the subject of וַיְהִי. The parallel clauses describe evening coming and then morning coming, in sequence on the third day.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־.

analysis.evidence: The parallel clauses וַיְהִי עֶרֶב and וַיְהִי בֹקֶר pair evening with morning in the account of the third day.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The marked וַיְהִי has בֹקֶר as its subject. It parallels וַיְהִי עֶרֶב, narrating the arrival of morning after evening on the third day.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: The parallel clauses וַיְהִי עֶרֶב and וַיְהִי בֹקֶר pair evening with morning in the account of the third day. בֹקֶר is the subject of the second וַיְהִי.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The ordinal שְׁלִישִׁי (‘third’) modifies יוֹם, counting the day marked by the evening and morning.
In יוֹם שְׁלִישִׁי, the adjective agrees with יוֹם in gender and number and identifies the day as the third in the creation sequence.
analysis.morphology: Ordinal adjective, masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.
